name: ponytail
description: Makes your AI agent think like the laziest senior dev in the room. The best code is the code you never wrote.
readmeExcerpt:
Ponytail

He says nothing. He writes one line. It works.

Ponytail 5: rebuilt from the ground up.
-53% code · -41% time · -26% cost · -45% tokens
And yet: 98% of risky logic ships with a test. Without Ponytail: 68%.
Benchmarked in Claude Code, the same agent with and without the skill: 39 tasks including a real FastAPI + React repo, Opus 5.5, 5 runs each. Details.

Español · 한국어 · 简体中文 · 日本語

---

## Already built with Ponytail --- You know him. Long ponytail. Oval glasses. Has been at the company longer than the version control. You show him fifty lines; he looks at them, says nothing, and replaces them with one. Ponytail puts him inside your AI agent. ## Numbers

Two things the chart does not show: in a blind comparison, Ponytail 5's replies beat the previous Ponytail's 110 to 67. And on the six security tasks (SQL injection, path traversal, forged tokens, rate limiting, malformed CSV rows, caching) it passed all 30 runs: less code, no less safe. Method, per-task tables and limits: [benchmarks/results/2026-10-07-agentic.md](benchmarks/results/2026-10-07-agentic.md). **The rule was never "fewest tokens."** It is: write only what the task needs, and never cut validation, error handling, security, or accessibility. The code ends up small because it is necessary, not golfed. Lower cost and latency are a side effect. ## Before / after

You ask for a date picker. Without Ponytail, the agent installs a date picker library or builds a whole calendar by hand: 335 lines. Ponytail 5 first looks at what is already there: the repo has an `Input` component, and every browser has a date picker. It puts the two together. 10 lines. More survivors in [examples/](examples/). ## The review, rebuilt

`/ponytail-review` used to look only for code to cut. Now it reviews like the senior dev who gets paged when it breaks: it reads the code your change touches, not just the diff, and checks bugs, security, real load, missing tests, speed, and what to cut. Each finding says what the code does, what goes wrong, how to fix it, and what happens if you don't. ## The audit, rebuilt

`/ponytail-audit` runs the same checks on the whole repo. It maps the code first: entry points, how data moves, what load the project expects. Then it ranks what it finds and tells you what to fix first. The old audit only listed what to delete. ## New in 5.3: the band

In Claude Code, ponytail now shows a band above the prompt: what the current task costs, how many tokens and how much agent time it used, how often it reused existing code instead of writing new code, and whether the tests passed after the last change. Its buttons switch the level, run `/ponytail-review` or `/ponytail-audit`, copy the task as Markdown, and fold the band into one line. Don't want it? `/ponytail band` hides it, the same command brings it back. Needs Claude Code 2.1.290 or later, in the terminal or the desktop app. It does not show in the VS Code chat panel, cloud sessions or `claude -p`.

**Board** opens a local page with every task across your projects: cost, agent time and tokens over time, every session with its tests, and the days you worked. By default, everything stays on your machine, in `~/.config/ponytail/band/`. `/ponytail band import` adds your past Claude Code sessions to it, with their cost, agent time and tokens. ## How it works

The ladder runs *after* it understands the problem, not instead of it: it reads the code the change touches and traces the real flow before picking a rung. Lazy about the solution, never about reading. Lazy, not negligent: trust-boundary validation, data-loss handling, security, and accessibility are never on the chopping block. Logic with a branch, a loop, a parser, money or security leaves one small test behind. Every reply ends with what was skipped or not checked and any risk you should know. ## The prompt Ponytail is one prompt: [`skills/ponytail/SKILL.md`](skills/ponytail/SKILL.md). The compact version, for agents that read a rules file, is [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md). Everything else in this repo loads that prompt into different agents. ## Install **Claude Code**, as two separate prompts: ``` /plugin marketplace add DietrichGebert/ponytail ``` ``` /plugin install ponytail@ponytail ``` **Codex:** ```bash codex plugin marketplace add DietrichGebert/ponytail codex plugin add ponytail@ponytail ``` Then open `/hooks` in Codex, trust its two lifecycle hooks, and start a new thread. **Any other agent:** copy [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) into your project, or ask your agent to install [`skills/ponytail/SKILL.md`](skills/ponytail/SKILL.md) as a skill. Step by step for Copilot, Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini and the rest: **[INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md)**. That was it. He'd be proud. He won't say it. Active every session, with a handful of commands (see [Commands](#commands)). `/ponytail ultra` exists for when the codebase has wronged you personally. Startup and mode-change text shows the current mode. Only install ponytail from `DietrichGebert/ponytail` on GitHub or `@dietrichgebert/ponytail` on npm. It never ships `.exe` or `.dll` files; a copy that does is not mine. ## Commands | Command | What it does | |---------|--------------| | `/ponytail [lite \| full \| ultra \| off]` | Set the intensity, or turn it off. No argument switches ponytail on at the default level if it is off, and otherwise reports the current level. | | `/ponytail band [on \| off]` | Claude Code only: hide or show the band above the prompt. No argument switches it. The level stays. | | `/ponytail band import` | Claude Code only: add your past Claude Code sessions to the board, with their cost, agent time and tokens. | | `/ponytail-review` | Review the current diff like the senior dev who gets paged when it breaks: bugs, security, real load, risky code without a test, slow paths, and what to cut. Each finding says what the code does, what goes wrong, how to fix it, and what happens if you don't. Name a target in plain words to narrow or widen it:

releases.name: v5.3.2
releases.body:
Ponytail 5.3.2 brings your old sessions to the board. `/ponytail band import` reads your past Claude Code sessions once and adds them with their cost, agent time and tokens, so you can compare them with today's. The board also shows which model each session used.

releases.name: v5.3.1
releases.body:
Ponytail 5.3.1 fixes the band from 5.3. Other mods above the Claude Code prompt now show below the band instead of disappearing, and on Windows the band finds its files without `HOME` and writes the task ledger and board without `mkdir`. Thanks to @AllDmeat and @mohofo7 for the fixes, and to @tomkor and @1410822048 for the reports.


## What's Changed
* fix(band): stack other mods' bands below ours instead of replacing them by @AllDmeat in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/1146
* fix(band): fall back to USERPROFILE when HOME is unset by @mohofo7 in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/1144
* fix(band): write the ledger and board without mkdir by @mohofo7 in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/1145
* chore: release v5.3.1 by @DietrichGebert in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/1147

## New Contributors

releases.name: v5.2.0
releases.body:
Mostly fixes for the level you pick. It now survives context compaction instead of falling back to the default, and on macOS the hooks can no longer lose their output, so the ruleset always arrives.

Also in here: the Cursor installer leaves hooks.json files it doesn't understand alone and no longer removes your own hooks with a similar name, OpenCode doesn't get stuck in review anymore and supports `/ponytail default`, pi completes `/ponytail` arguments, and OMP starts new sessions at the default level. Thanks to everyone who sent fixes!


## What's Changed
* fix(bench): a crashed cell no longer crashes the run summary by @DietrichGebert in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/1110
* docs: manual Hermes install until Hermes fixes its plugin.json check by @DietrichGebert in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/1111
* feat(pi-extension): autocomplete /ponytail arguments by @ruttybob in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/1080
* fix(hooks): write hook output synchronously so process.exit cannot drop it by @DietrichGebert in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/1112
* fix: preserve invalid Cursor hook configurations during install by @ac198

releases.name: v5.1.1
releases.body:
A fix release. The big one is the codebase map from 5.0: a repo could slip its own text into the hidden session context, and a symlink in the repo could hang the session start until the ruleset never arrived. Both are fixed, and the map now has a one-second limit, so the rules always load.

Also in here: hooks work again when a project pins an old Node, three fixes for OpenCode 2 (compaction cache, command arguments, mention highlights), and `/ponytail-debt` now skips everything in `.gitignore`. Thanks to everyone who sent reports and fixes this week.


## What's Changed
* fix(bench): completeness judge checks what the agent actually delivered by @DietrichGebert in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/1094
* docs: link the bounty program in the README by @DietrichGebert in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/1093
* docs: README asks for Ponytail stories instead of bounties by @DietrichGebert in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/1095
* docs: stories banner in the README by @DietrichGebert in https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/pull/1096
* fix(hooks): keep hook launchers loadable on Node 12 (#1072) by @paul-vd in https://github.com/Dietrich

Commands

Command What it does
/ponytail [lite | full | ultra | off] Set the intensity, or turn it off. No argument switches ponytail on at the default level if it is off, and otherwise reports the current level.
/ponytail band [on | off] Claude Code only: hide or show the band above the prompt. No argument switches it. The level stays.
/ponytail band import Claude Code only: add your past Claude Code sessions to the board, with their cost, agent time and tokens.
/ponytail-review Review the current diff like the senior dev who gets paged when it breaks: bugs, security, real load, risky code without a test, slow paths, and what to cut. Each finding says what the code does, what goes wrong, how to fix it, and what happens if you don't. Name a target in plain words to narrow or widen it: uncommitted, staged, branch, or a PR link.
/ponytail-audit The same check for the whole repo, most important first.
/ponytail-debt Harvest the shortcut: comments you've deferred into a ledger, so "later" doesn't become "never".
/ponytail-gain Show the measured impact scoreboard (less code, less cost, more speed) from the benchmark.
/ponytail-help Quick reference for the commands above.

Commands need a skill-capable host (Claude Code, Codex, Devin CLI, OpenCode, Gemini, Antigravity CLI, pi, Hermes Agent, Qoder, Grok Build). In Codex CLI and the IDE extension they're skills under the plugin's namespace; invoke with $ponytail:ponytail-review. Cursor with the hooks gets /ponytail level switching only, typed as a plain message. The instruction-only adapters (Cursor's rule file, Windsurf, Cline, Copilot, Kiro, Antigravity's AGENTS.md fallback) load the always-on ruleset without the commands.

FAQ

Does it need a config file? No. An optional ~/.config/ponytail/config.json or PONYTAIL_DEFAULT_MODE env var can set the default level, but nothing is required.

Why does it write shortcut: comments? They mark a deliberate shortcut and when to revisit it, and /ponytail-debt collects them into a ledger. Want another word, or none? Say so in your project's CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md, then run /ponytail-debt <your word>.

What if I really need the 120-line cache class? You don't. Insist anyway and he'll build it. Slowly. Correctly. While looking at you.

Does it scale? The code you never wrote scales infinitely. Zero bugs, zero CVEs, 100% uptime since forever.

Why "ponytail"? You know exactly why.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A specialized proxy tool designed to extract and organize structured data from unstructured LLM responses.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Ponytail operates as an intelligent proxy layer that intercepts and processes responses from Large Language Models before they reach the client application. It solves the critical problem of LLM output unpredictability by rigorously parsing unstructured text and forcing it into strict, predefined JSON schemas. The tool utilizes advanced regex mapping and iterative validation loops to ensure the final output strictly adheres to the requested data structure. By acting as an intermediary API, it abstracts the complex prompt engineering and error handling required for reliable data extraction. This allows developers to treat stochastic language models as predictable, structured data sources.
keyFeatures: Strict schema enforcement: Validates and coerces unstructured LLM text outputs into rigorously defined JSON structures.
Proxy architecture: Sits between the application and the LLM provider, providing a seamless, drop-in replacement for standard API calls.
Iterative self-correction: Automatically reprompts the underlying model if the initial output fails to pass schema validation constraints.
Advanced parsing algorithms: Utilizes custom regex and heuristic extraction to salvage valid data payloads from noisy, conversational model responses.
Provider agnostic design: Interacts cleanly with multiple LLM backends including OpenAI, Anthropic, and local open-source models.

useCases.title: Reliable Data Extraction
useCases.description: Extract structured entities like dates, names, and financial figures from messy OCR text without worrying about broken JSON syntax.

useCases.title: API Backend Modernization
useCases.description: Route legacy application requests through the proxy to instantly enrich responses with LLM-generated, strictly formatted metadata.

useCases.title: Automated Content Tagging
useCases.description: Process incoming user feedback and guarantee the LLM returns an array of specific, valid category tags for a database.

useCases.title: Workflow Automation
useCases.description: Ensure multi-step AI agents receive perfectly formatted JSON payloads between steps to prevent catastrophic parsing failures.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Backend developers, AI engineers, and data scientists building production applications that rely on structured data from LLMs. It is essential for teams struggling with unpredictable API responses breaking their JSON parsers.
